channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Os dois fatores que pesaram contra Flávio Bolsonaro na nova pesquisa Quaest sobre eleição presidencial
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll found that Flávio Bolsonaro lost electoral potential due to his rapprochement with Daniel Vorcaro for funding the film 'Dark Horse' and his actions alongside the U.S. government, particularly in pushing to label PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist groups. Although 65% of voters believe he erred in seeking Vorcaro's support, 76% say it won’t change their vote. His damaged image helps explain Lula’s lead in the polls.

item.title: Lula e Sheinbaum discutem comércio e parceria entre Petrobras e Pemex
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum discussed bilateral trade and a potential agreement between Petrobras and Pemex during a videoconference on June 10, 2026. They also reaffirmed support for ending the U.S. embargo on Cuba, endorsed Michelle Bachelet’s candidacy for UN Secretary-General, and wished Mexico success in hosting the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which opened on June 11. The call included Foreign Ministers Mauro Vieira and Roberto Velasco and emphasized energy cooperation, biofuels, and updating the bilateral commercial framework.

item.title: Lula diz que empresários “aprenderam” a respeitar acordos ambientais
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazilian business leaders have learned to respect environmental agreements, recognizing that non-compliance leads to economic losses and hinders product commercialization. He emphasized the productive sector's evolution toward sustainable practices and said Brazil has regained international environmental credibility due to the efforts of environmentalists, regulatory agencies, and former Environment Minister Marina Silva.

item.title: O dado das pesquisas que pode acender alerta para Lula mesmo com queda de Flávio
item.description: The decline of Flávio Bolsonaro in 2026 election polls did not translate into electoral gains for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, whose support levels remained stable. According to Murilo Hidalgo of Paraná Pesquisas, the votes lost by Flávio were captured by other center-right candidates, including Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, and Joaquim Barbosa, showing that Lula failed to expand his base despite the senator's setbacks.

item.title: Governo amplia proteção ambiental e prepara recuperação de florestas
item.description: President Lula announced a package of environmental measures on World Environment Day, including the creation of new conservation units, expansion of protected areas, enactment of the National Policy for Caatinga Recovery, and streamlining of the National Environment Fund transfers to states and municipalities for wildfire prevention. He noted Brazil recorded less than 1 million hectares of deforestation in 2025 (984,700 ha) — an unprecedented feat — and said the country is now proactively prepared to face extreme climate events like El Niño.

item.title: Alvos de medidas de Trump, presidentes de Brasil e México reiteram defesa da não interferência estrangeira
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum reaffirmed their commitment to multilateralism, international law, and non-interference in a videoconference amid new U.S. tariff threats against Brazil and Mexico. They also voiced support for ending the U.S. embargo on Cuba, backing Michelle Bachelet’s bid for UN Secretary-General, and advancing the VI Binational Mexico-Brazil Commission. The discussion took place as the USTR recommended tariffs on Brazil over alleged unfair practices involving PIX, ethanol, anti-deforestation policies, and intellectual property.

item.title: Marco Civil da Internet: Toffoli começa a votar nos embargos e traz mudanças na tese
item.description: Justice Dias Toffoli, rapporteur of the STF in the judgment of the embargos against the Marco Civil da Internet, introduced innovations in his partial vote, maintaining subjective liability of platforms for third-party content, except in marketplaces where objective CDC liability applies. He proposes to further mitigate the application of Article 19, making liability dependent on the level of platform interference in content circulation, with neutral providers (like Wikipedia) requiring judicial decision to be held liable. Toffoli also suggested a 60-day adaptation period for big techs and that the new thesis apply only to actions filed after the publication of the judgment's record.

item.title: Governo avalia ir ao STF contra pauta-bomba de R$ 140 bi
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that the Senate-approved rural debt renegotiation project could cost the National Treasury R$140 billion in the coming years, exceeding the government's fiscal capacity. He said the government will seek amendments in the Chamber of Deputees, may recommend presidential vetoes, and could challenge the project in the Supreme Federal Court if it violates the Fiscal Responsibility Law.

item.title: “Crime de adulto, pena de adulto”, diz Zema
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo-MG) celebrated the approval of PEC 32/2015 by the Chamber's Constitution and Justice Committee, which lowers the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16 for serious crimes. In a post on X, he defended the measure with the phrase 'Crime of adulthood, punishment of adulthood'.

item.title: Diante de pesquisas desfavoráveis, oposição a Lula ainda debate o que fazer
item.description: The opposition to Lula struggles with strategic shortcomings by over-relying on opinion polls, leading to candidate choices like Flávio Bolsonaro driven more by anti-Lula sentiment than substantive platforms. This short-term focus leaves center-right groups exposed when polls shift, especially in a volatile environment where external factors such as inflation and high interest rates could undermine the incumbent regardless of the challenger.

item.title: Lula abre seis pontos de vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno, indica Quaest
item.description: Lula leads a potential runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro with 44% voting intention, compared to 38% for the PL senator, according to the Genial/Quaest poll. The six-point advantage reflects a consolidation of support for the president in a polarized scenario. The poll was reported by O Antagonista.

item.title: Veto da UE à carne brasileira foi por falha de ministério, diz Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, former governor of Goiás and pre-candidate for president from the PSD, blamed the Ministry of Agriculture for bureaucratic failure in clearing Brazilian beef exports to the European Union, which led to a ban effective September 3, impacting over R$9 billion in Brazilian agribusiness. He attended a meeting at the EU Delegation in Brasília with Senator Nelsinho Trad and PSD national president Gilberto Kassab, urging the EU to reconsider restrictions that prohibit antimicrobial use for growth promotion in livestock. Caiado advocated for an international perspective, arguing that domestic issues should not be solved by penalizing other nations, and noted that other Mercosul countries remain authorized to export beef to the EU.

item.title: Senado aprova pauta-bomba que custará R$ 140 bi aos cofres públicos
item.description: The Senate symbolically approved Bill 5.122/2023, authorizing the use of R$ 140 billion from the Pre-Salt Social Fund and other surpluses to renegotiate rural debts of producers affected by climate and geopolitical events. While Finance Minister Dario Durigan defended the measure as necessary to support the agribusiness sector, critics warn it risks public finances amid global uncertainty. The bill returns to the Chamber of Deputies after Senate amendments.

item.title: Joaquim Barbosa deve quebrar silêncio sobre pré-candidatura na próxima semana, diz presidente do DC
item.description: The president of the Christian Democracy party, João Caldas, states that Joaquim Barbosa's pre-candidacy for president will prosper, despite the former STF minister's current silence. Caldas expects Barbosa to begin speaking with the press next week and then take to the streets to launch his campaign. However, polls show Barbosa has only 1% of national voting intentions, with limited support concentrated in the Southeast (2%) and negligible presence in the South and Northeast.

item.title: Nunes Marques vota por manter pesquisa suspensa, mas pedido de vista adia decisão no TSE
item.description: The judgment on the release of the AtlasIntel presidential poll was interrupted at the TSE after rapporteur Minister Kassio Nunes Marques voted to maintain the suspension of the survey. A request for vista delayed the final plenary decision, keeping the poll suspended for now.

item.title: Durigan diz que governo avalia vetar renegociação de dívidas rurais caso projeto passe na Câmara; Senado aprovou proposta
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the government is considering a veto or STF action if the rural debt renegotiation bill passes the Chamber, after the Senate approved it with amendments. Dubbed a 'budget bomb,' the measure could cost between R$120 billion and R$140 billion, increasing public debt. Despite government opposition, Senate President Davi Alcolumbre brought it to vote without executive support.

item.title: Como está a disputa entre Keiko Fujimori e Sánchez entre peruanos de 11 capitais brasileiras
item.description: In Peru's presidential runoff, Roberto Sánchez (left) leads nationally with 50,03% of the vote against Keiko Fujimori (right) at 49,97%, with 97.9% of ballots counted. However, among Peruvians residing in Brazil, Fujimori leads with 55.7% of the vote across 11 state capitals, winning in nine of them, including São Paulo, where the race remains tight at 50.8% to 49.2%.

item.title: Senado aprova 'pauta-bomba' e negociação de dívidas rurais avança no Congresso; Fazenda calcula impacto de R$ 140 bilhões
item.description: The Senate approved a bill allowing rural producers to renegotiate their debts, expanding the scope beyond its original focus on those affected by public calamities. The Lula government opposes the measure, with the Ministry of Finance estimating a fiscal impact of R$ 140 billion by 2027, and had sought to block it but failed to reach an agreement with senators. The bill, already passed by the Chamber of Deputies, must now return for a new vote due to Senate amendments, leaving room for future negotiations or a provisional measure.

item.title: Senado aprova renegociação de dívidas de produtores rurais; governo é contra e vê projeto como pauta-bomba
item.description: The Senate approved a bill to renegotiate rural debts for producers affected by extreme weather and international geopolitical conflicts, despite opposition from the Lula government, which estimates a fiscal impact of up to R$ 140 billion. Senate rapporteur Renan Calheiros claims the cost will be lower, around R$ 120 billion over ten years, limited to overdue debts. The bill must return to the Chamber of Deputies for a new vote before presidential sanction.

item.title: Senado apresenta sua TV 3.0 em encontro de emissoras da Rede Legislativa
item.description: The Senate officially launched its TV 3.0 during the Legislative Network Radio and TV Meeting 2026 in Brasília, emphasizing the integration of open broadcast and streaming on a single device. Developed for over a year, the technology aims to expand the reach of legislative broadcasters, including in areas without open signal, and strengthen public communication as a tool for promoting citizenship and democracy, particularly ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Renan Santos descarta aliança com Aécio: “Não faz sentido”
item.description: Renan Santos, a pre-candidate for the Presidency of the Republic, ruled out an alliance with Aécio Neves, federal deputy and national president of the PSDB, stating that such a partnership "does not make sense." He avoided elaborating but suggested the answer would be "crude" if pressed further. The statement was made on Wednesday, the 10th, and attracted media attention.

item.title: Após queda em pesquisas, Flávio vai visitar Bolsonaro neste sábado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) will visit former President Jair Bolsonaro this Saturday, following authorization from Minister Alexandre de Moraes, amid declining poll numbers. A Quaest poll shows he is six points behind Lula in a potential runoff, with 38% versus Lula’s 44%. The visit comes after a scandal involving an alleged request for funds from banker Daniel Vorcaro to produce a biopic about Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Fachin critica tentativas de questionar atos de autoridades brasileiras no exterior e faz alerta sobre ingerência
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin warned against efforts to challenge acts of Brazilian authorities in foreign tribunals, stating such actions may produce cross-border consequences and defending respect for national institutional independence. He stressed that cooperation between democracies does not justify interference in sovereign internal affairs and linked judicial independence to the protection of constitutional democracy.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Senado inspeciona códigos-fonte dos sistemas eleitorais no TSE
item.description: The Federal Senate inspected the source code of the electoral systems used by the TSE in Brasília as part of the Democratic Transparency Cycle. The verification, held on Wednesday (10), included opening an electronic voting machine to demonstrate its internal operation and presenting the software by Rodrigo Coimbra, head of the TSE’s Electronic Voting Section, who emphasized the system’s security, transparency, and auditability. União Brasil had conducted the first inspection in May.

item.title: A nova ofensiva do PT no Supremo contra o dinheiro de ‘Dark Horse’
item.description: The PT has requested Minister Flávio Dino and the Federal Police to open a criminal investigation into the funding of the film 'Dark Horse', a pro-Jair Bolsonaro propaganda piece. The party alleges that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro negotiated approximately R$134 million in transfers with banker Daniel Vorcaro, of which around R$61 million were reportedly sent to a U.S.-based fund managed by an advisor to Eduardo Bolsonaro, and suspects illicit use of parliamentary amendments and possible caixa dois.

item.title: Equipe econômica recebeu sinalização que Alcolumbre irá barrar pautas-bomba, mas receio permanece após derrotas
item.description: The economic team received signals that Senate President Davi Alcolumbre intends to block the voting of 'bomb bills' in plenary, but concern remains after recent defeats in Senate committees, including the PEC on Central Bank autonomy and proposals for community health agents and a national minimum wage for doctors. The government fears the Senate will use these measures to weaken the Executive in an election year, especially following the rift between Alcolumbre and Lula over the rejection of Jorge Messias’ STF nomination.

item.title: Senado aprova indicação de Benedito Gonçalves para uma vaga no CNJ
item.description: The Senate approved the nomination of Minister Benedito Gonçalves from the Superior Tribunal of Justice (STJ) to a vacancy in the National Council of Justice (CNJ) by a vote of 53 to 16. Rapporteur Senator Cid Gomes advocated for expanding the CNJ’s authority to include oversight of the Supreme Federal Court, stating this aligns with the original intent of the 1988 Constituent Assembly. Gonçalves, appointed to the STJ by Lula in 2008, holds a law degree from UFRJ, a specialization in civil procedure from UnB-CJF, and a master’s from Estácio de Sá.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio destaca subida na intenção de voto espontânea medida pela Quaest
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) presidential pre-campaign welcomed the rise in spontaneous voting intention to 17% in the Quaest poll, three percentage points above the previous survey. The team views the result as a sign of growth in the 2026 presidential race. The data was released on October 6, 2026.

item.title: Governo registra o Pix como marca de alto renome no INPI
item.description: The Brazilian federal government registered Pix as a high-repute trademark with the INPI, granting extended protection across all economic sectors. The announcement was made by Minister Márcio Elias Rosa during a meeting of the Conselhão, in response to U.S. allegations that Pix unfairly harms companies like Visa and Mastercard.

item.title: Torcida brasileira: pesquisa revela como os fãs se comportam
item.description: Betsson Brasil's research shows Brazilians have a deep passion for football, with 73% preferring it over other sports and 168.6 million fans — more than the total population of Germany and France. During the World Cup, engagement extends beyond stadiums, with adjusted work and school schedules, street decorations, and celebrations in bars and homes. Brazilian fans react instantly to goals, celebrating immediately, driven by strong emotional identification; a Radiology study found the brain interprets a goal as a personal achievement, activating social identity centers.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: Lula abre 44% a 38% contra Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno, aponta Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva leading with 44% of voting intentions against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro at 38% in a simulated 2026 presidential runoff. This gives Lula a six-point advantage, breaking a previous scenario of technical tie or Bolsonarist lead. The findings were discussed on the Papo Antagonista program and indicate a notable shift in voter sentiment.

item.title: Contra Lula, a direita preferiu um asno manco a um cavalo de corrida
item.description: The right lost its strong candidate Tarcísio de Freitas and now backs Flávio Bolsonaro, who is trailing far behind Lula in the polls. Genial/Quaest shows Lula at 44% and Flávio at 38%, a 6-point gap that could widen to 8 points or 8 million votes. Independent voters are shifting to Lula due to policies like Desenrola and Trump's tariffs, leaving the right in a weakened position.

item.title: Homem tenta obter habeas corpus para Bolsonaro no STJ, mas Kassio barra
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques of the STF rejected a habeas corpus petition filed by an individual on behalf of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who claimed the STF and STJ lacked jurisdiction over the coup plot case. The minister emphasized that Supreme Court jurisprudence does not permit habeas corpus against acts of justices, chambers, or the full Court, and dismissed the appeal. The argument that the Superior Military Tribunal had jurisdiction was previously rejected by the STF.

item.title: Sob Lula, dividendos de bancos são 24% maiores do que sob Bolsonaro
item.description: Between 2023 and March 2026, Brazil's five largest banks distributed R$ 195.7 billion in dividends and interest on equity, 24.2% more than the total paid between 2019 and 2022. Itaú Unibanco led distributions with R$ 48.9 billion in 2025 alone, while BTG Pactual showed the highest proportional growth at 149.4%. The increase reflects the financial sector's high profitability driven by elevated interest rates and record results.

item.title: Novas pesquisas reforçam vantagem de Lula sobre Flávio Bolsonaro no Rali após caso Master; veja os números
item.description: The Rali poll aggregator shows Lula (PT) leading Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the 2026 presidential runoff with 45% to 40.6%, following the Master Bank scandal and Trump-era tariffs on Brazilian goods. Lula gained ground after Flávio briefly led in May, losing support among independent voters where Lula now leads by 13 points (37% to 24%). The trend is confirmed by recent Datafolha, Genial/Quaest and Meio/Ideia surveys.

item.title: Lula anuncia pacote de ações e investimentos para agenda ambiental
item.description: President Lula announced a package of environmental measures, including the sanctioning of the National Policy for Caatinga Recovery Law, the launch of the Recaatingar Program with an initial R$ 60 million from BNDES and BNB, allocation of R$ 2 billion for Ibama and ICMBio in the Doce River basin, release of R$ 834 million from the Climate Fund for native vegetation restoration, signing of a R$ 270 million donation from the United Kingdom to the Amazon Fund, disbursement of R$ 393 million for the Restaura Amazônia program, and a R$ 370 million donation to the ARPA Communities program. He also regulated the National Policy for Payment for Environmental Services (PSA).

item.title: ‘TariFlávio’ se consolida como arma da oposição contra Flávio no meio digital
item.description: The Brazilian left uses the term 'Tariflávio' to blame Flávio Bolsonaro for a potential new U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, accusing him of subservience to Donald Trump and endangering the Pix payment system to benefit American financial firms. The right responds defensively, shifting blame to Lula’s government, defending Pix as a Bolsonaro-era achievement, and linking the tariffs to social media censorship and failures in combating corruption and organized crime, while maintaining an offensive on public safety by linking Lula to organized crime and promoting Flávio as the leader in designating PCC and CV as terrorist organizations.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest: o eleitor que pode salvar — ou afundar — a candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Independent voters are emerging as decisive in a potential runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, with Lula gaining ground while the senator loses support among this group. From April to June, Lula rose from 26% to 37% among independents, while Bolsonaro fell from 33% to 24%, driven by negative news including his ties to Daniel Vorcaro and the U.S. tariff policy. According to Quaest, independents — comprising roughly one-third of the electorate — often determine election outcomes due to their ideological fluidity.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula faz anúncios sobre o meio ambiente
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced a set of environmental measures in observance of World Environment Day, including the signing of a law, creation and expansion of federal Conservation Units, investments through the Climate Fund and Amazon Fund, and recognition of environmental services provided by nature protectors. The event took place in the Noble Hall of the Planalto Palace, attended by Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and Environment Minister João Paulo Capobianco.

item.title: Desgaste com os EUA é tema central de reunião de Lula com o Conselhão
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva emphasized trade tensions with the United States as a central theme in the 7th plenary meeting of the CDESS, challenging U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods and demanding an urgent study on American workers’ wages and rights to justify Brazil’s stance. He referenced the USTR report targeting Pix, digital trade, ethanol, and deforestation, stating Brazil will not accept measures undermining its dignity and economic sovereignty. Ministers Mauro Vieira (Foreign Affairs) and José Guimarães (Institutional Relations) affirmed a firm defense of Brazil’s commercial interests, while Dario Durigan (Finance) asserted that Brazil is recognized as a global leader in economics, environment, and fuels, despite ongoing friction with Washington.

item.title: Lula sugere existência de interferência externa em protestos no México
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva suggested that ongoing teacher protests in Mexico may involve external interference, drawing parallels to the 2013 protests in Brazil that, he claimed, paved the way for the rise of the far-right. Lula said he plans to speak with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum about the situation. The CNTE, Mexico’s education workers’ union, has been on strike since June 1, demanding the repeal of a pension reform, reinstatement of fired teachers, and a 100% salary increase, having blocked traffic on the avenue leading to Estadio Azteca, where the 2026 World Cup opening ceremony is scheduled.

item.title: Lula diz que não aceitará taxação dos EUA por ‘respeito aos trabalhadores’
item.description: Lula stated he will not accept the proposed U.S. tariffs, citing a lack of respect for Brazilian workers and demanding a comparative study of wages and labor rights between the two countries. He linked U.S. trade pressure to unfair practices and potential external influence behind the rise of the far-right in Mexico, drawing parallels to events in Brazil in 2013. He also defended social spending for the poor, criticizing financial markets for opposing such investments without accounting for the cost of inaction.

item.title: O dado que mais animou equipe de Lula em nova pesquisa da corrida presidencial
item.description: The Quaest poll boosted Lula’s re-election campaign, showing his support among undecided voters rose from 29% to 37%, while Flávio Bolsonaro fell from 31% to 24%. Improvements in approval ratings and among evangelicals were also noted, validating the strategy of linking Flávio to Daniel Vorcaro and opposing Trump’s tariffs. The team sees room for further growth by emphasizing these issues.

item.title: Neymar pode passar Rivaldo e tem disputa acirrada com Cristiano Ronaldo
item.description: Neymar could surpass Rivaldo, Ademir Menezes, and Jairzinho in Brazil’s World Cup goal involvement list if he maintains his current form in 2026. With 11 involvements (8 goals, 3 assists), he exceeds Cristiano Ronaldo (10) but trails Messi (21) and Mbappé (14) among international stars. Pelé (21) and Ronaldo (18) remain the undisputed leaders in Brazilian World Cup history.

item.title: Agenda Legislativa Mulheres do Brasil prioriza cotas femininas no Legislativo e orçamento voltado às mulheres
item.description: The Women's Legislative Agenda of Brazil, launched in a solemn session of the National Congress, prioritizes the approval of gender quotas in legislative bodies, including PLP 112/21, which reserves 20% of federal, state, and municipal legislative seats for women, and PLP 218/23, which establishes a gender-sensitive budget in the federal public administration. The initiative aims to correct women's underrepresentation, as they comprise 51.5% of the population but hold only 18% of seats in the Chamber of Deputies and 19% in the Senate.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula preocupado com o ‘Não vai ter Copa’ no México
item.description: President Lula compared the protests in Mexico led by the National Education Workers' Union (CNTE) to the June 2013 demonstrations in Brazil, suggesting they may be subject to external interference. He expressed concern that the 'Not Going to Have the World Cup' movement in Mexico could be influenced by external forces, similar to what occurred in Brazil ahead of the 2014 World Cup.

item.title: Urgência constitucional de Lula deve impor lentidão ainda maior na Câmara
item.description: The constitutional urgency imposed by the Lula government on the bill to end the 6×1 work schedule is slowing down proceedings in the Chamber of Deputies, as it blocks the plenary agenda until withdrawn. Although in-person sessions are expected next week, caucuses may request remote work, and the following week deputies are likely to return to their electoral bases. The move also aims to pressure Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to advance the PEC ending the 6×1 schedule, which remains undispatched to the CCJ.

item.title: PT pede investigação se orçamento de 'Dark Horse' virou caixa 2 da campanha de Flávio
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) has requested an investigation by the Federal Police and the Supreme Federal Court into the production of the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays the life of former President Jair Bolsonaro, over allegations that part of its budget was diverted to illegally fund Flávio Bolsonaro's electoral campaign, potentially constituting illicit campaign financing (caixa 2).

item.title: Trump não deportou 'diplomatas petistas' dos EUA; imagem é IA
item.description: Social media posts falsely claim that Donald Trump deported 'petista diplomats' from the U.S. and that they recorded a video crying and blaming Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The claim is false and has been debunked as AI-generated content. There is no evidence of such deportations or the referenced video.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia repudia censura e cassa decisão que derrubou matéria sobre ex-governador do Amazonas
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Cármen Lúcia overturned a decision by the Amazonas Court of Justice that ordered the removal of a critical article about former governor Wilson Lima, labeling it judicial censorship. She directed the TJ-AM to reassess the case with full respect for press freedom and the right to inform and be informed.
